name: Mandarin Oriental, Geneva
positioning: Five-star city hotel on the right bank of the Rhône River in Geneva, opened in 1950 as the Hôtel du Rhône
best_for: Travelers who want a Rhône-side base within walking distance of Geneva's Old Town and the Jet d'Eau
Diners drawn to Japanese cuisine at SACHI and Ottolenghi's vegetable-focused Mediterranean cooking
Families who want two connecting rooms

facts.text: Mandarin Oriental, Geneva is located at Quai Turrettini 1, on the right bank of the Rhône River.
The hotel is within walking distance of the Old Town, the Jet d’Eau and major shopping streets like the Rue du Rhône.
Mandarin Oriental, Geneva is a five-star hotel.
The hotel opened on July 14, 1950 as the Hôtel du Rhône.
The hotel has been part of the Mandarin Oriental Hotel Group since 2000.
SACHI is a Japanese restaurant at the hotel.
SACHI serves the black cod with yuzu miso sauce.
MO Bar offers cocktails and tapas.
In-room dining is available at all times.
The fitness centre has TechnoGym equipment.
The fitness area has a separate sauna and hammam for men and women.
Ambassade Biologique Recherche at the hotel offers personalised face, body and scalp treatments.

highlights.text: Ottolenghi Geneva is Ottolenghi’s first restaurant outside of the UK.
Ottolenghi Geneva celebrates vegetables from root to tip, with a focus on fermentation and cooking over fire.
The Omakase Bar at SACHI is designed for ten guests, who can watch the chefs prepare each dish.
Forbes Travel Guide ranked MO Bar among the 58 best hotel bars in the world in 2025.
The Royal Terrace Suite occupies the hotel’s highest floor and has a terrace with views of snow-capped mountains, the Rhône River and Geneva’s Old Town.
The family rooms feature two connecting rooms.

considerations.text: The hotel is at the heart of Geneva’s business district.
MO Bar welcomes guests on a walk-in basis only and does not accept reservations.
Guests are encouraged to reserve a table in advance at the hotel’s restaurants.
WhataHotel notes that premium luxury pricing reflects Geneva’s high-cost destination.
